mainTopic: The order of the daily Temple services around the תמיד, and which offerings may come after the afternoon תמיד
overview: The amud opens by finishing a source for why the afternoon תמיד comes before the קרבן פסח: the פסח has two time-words, "בערב" and "בין הערבים", and the תמיד has only one. The גמרא asks why the קטרת and נרות, which also have only "בין הערבים", do not come before the פסח too. One ברייתא answers that the word "אותו" makes lighting the נרות the only service valid all night, and the קטרת is linked to the נרות. A second ברייתא disagrees and puts the order as תמיד, קטרת, נרות, פסח. That ברייתא reads "אותו" as excluding only the inside service, the קטרת, so the קטרת must already be burning when the נרות are lit. Next, a ברייתא teaches that only the קטרת comes before the morning תמיד. It also lists the few things allowed after the afternoon תמיד, including a מחוסר כפורים on ערב פסח, and רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא extends this to every day of the year. The גמרא asks how רבי ישמעאל's view fits with the מצוה of השלמה, and רב חסדא and רב פפא each give an answer. Questions about the אשם and the עולה follow, ending with the rule that a חטאת always comes before its עולה. רבא begins to answer that the עולה of a מצורע is different, and his proof verse continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The פסח comes after the תמיד because of its time-words
steps.stepSummary: The פסח is described with both "בערב" and "בין הערבים", while the תמיד has only "בין הערבים". So the פסח is brought after the תמיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Something the Torah describes with both "in the evening" and "in the afternoon" should be brought after something the Torah describes only with "in the afternoon", without "in the evening".
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes giving its source for why the afternoon תמיד is brought before the קרבן פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסח has an extra time-word, "בערב", which points later in the day. The תמיד has only "בין הערבים". So the תמיד is earlier, and the פסח must wait until after it.

keyTerms.meaning: in the afternoon, literally 'between the evenings'

phrases.aramaic: יְאוּחַר דָּבָר שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בּוֹ ״בָּעָרֶב״ וּ״בֵין הָעַרְבָּיִם״,
phrases.english: An item about which it says "in the evening" and "in the afternoon" should be later
phrases.notes: This refers to the קרבן פסח. See דברים טז:ו and שמות יב:ו.

phrases.english: than an item about which it does not say "in the evening"
phrases.notes: This refers to the afternoon תמיד.

phrases.english: but only "in the afternoon."
phrases.notes: במדבר כח:ד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This completes a derivation that began on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sacrifice with both "בערב" and "בין הערבים" comes after one that has only "בין הערבים". So the פסח comes after the תמיד.

steps.title: Then the קטרת and נרות should also come before the פסח
steps.stepSummary: The קטרת and the נרות are also described only with "בין הערבים". By the same reasoning, they too should come before the פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the incense and the lamps should also come before the פסח. The item described with "in the evening" and "in the afternoon" should be later than an item described only with "in the afternoon"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rule from Step 1. It shows that the rule would also force the קטרת and נרות to come before the פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse about the קטרת and נרות (שמות ל:ח) also says only "בין הערבים". So the same logic should put them before the פסח too. Yet the view being explained holds that the פסח comes before them, so the גמרא must explain why.

keyTerms.meaning: the incense burned on the inner altar

phrases.english: If so,
the incense and lamps should also come before the Pesach:

phrases.aramaic: יְאוּחַר דָּבָר שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בּוֹ ״בָּעָרֶב״ וּ״בֵין הָעַרְבָּיִם״,
phrases.english: an item about which it says "in the evening" and "in the afternoon" should be later
phrases.notes: The גמרא quotes the rule from Step 1 again, now aimed at a new case.

phrases.aramaic: לְדָבָר שֶׁלֹּא נֶאֱמַר בּוֹ אֶלָּא ״בֵּין הָעַרְבָּיִם״ בִּלְבַד!
phrases.english: than an item about which it says only "in the afternoon"!
phrases.notes: שמות ל:ח: "ובהעלות אהרן את הנרות בין הערבים יקטירנה".

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This challenges the rule from Step 1 by applying it to another case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that "בין הערבים" alone means a service comes earlier.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The קטרת and נרות share the same single time-word as the תמיד. So the rule would wrongly require them to come before the פסח too.

steps.title: The lamps are different because of the word אותו
steps.stepSummary: The נרות are an exception. The word "אותו" in their verse sets them apart.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because the Merciful One limited it with the word "it".
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It says the נרות are a special case, because the Torah singles them out with the word "אותו".
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general rule from Step 1 still stands. The נרות are simply an exception, created by an extra word in the verse. The קטרת goes along with the נרות, because שמות ל:ח links the two together. The following steps explain what "אותו" teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: the Merciful One, meaning the Torah
"it", here an extra word that limits

phrases.english: It is different there
since the Merciful One limited it with "it".
phrases.notes: The word comes from שמות כז:כא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers the challenge of Step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Exception from a limiting word in the verse
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The נרות and קטרת fall under the general time-word rule and should come before the פסח.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word "אותו" marks the נרות as a unique service, so they come last. The קטרת follows them.

steps.title: ברייתא: give the menorah enough oil for the whole night
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא begins. Its first reading is that "מערב עד בקר" teaches to put in enough oil to burn all night.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: "From evening until morning" means give it its measure of oil, so that it burns from evening until morning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support its answer. This first reading of the ברייתא is not yet the main point. It sets up the "דבר אחר" reading that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to this first reading, the phrase is about how much oil to use. It is not about timing. The reading that actually supports the תירוץ comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: as it was taught in a ברייתא

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this first reading is the proof for "אותו". The proof is the "דבר אחר" reading in the next step.

phrases.english: As it was taught: "From evening until morning" —
give it its measure
phrases.notes: About half a לוג of oil per lamp.

phrases.english: so that it burns from evening until morning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This introduces the source for the word "אותו" used in Step 3.

steps.title: Only the lamps are valid from evening until morning
steps.stepSummary: The "דבר אחר" reading teaches from "אותו" that lighting the נרות is the only service valid through the night.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: there is no service that is valid from evening until morning except this one alone. What is the reason? The verse says, "Aaron and his sons shall arrange it from evening until morning." It is valid from evening until morning, and nothing else is valid from evening until morning.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a second reading. This reading supports the גמרא's answer: the נרות are a unique nighttime service, marked off by the word "אותו".
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah could have written "יערכנו" as one word. Instead it wrote "יערך אותו" as two, and the separate word limits this law to the נרות alone. Since lighting the lamps is a service that belongs to the night, it is done at the end of the day, after the פסח, even though its verse says only "בין הערבים".
steps.whatToRemember: The general rule still holds: "בין הערבים" alone means earlier than "בערב" plus "בין הערבים". The נרות, and with them the קטרת, are an exception. The word "אותו" makes the lamps the only service valid all night, so they come last.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source that lighting the מנורה is the one Temple service allowed at night. This is why the daily order puts the lamps at the end of the afternoon.

phrases.english: Another explanation:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לְךָ עֲבוֹדָה שֶׁכְּשֵׁירָה מֵעֶרֶב עַד בּוֹקֶר
phrases.english: there is no service that is valid from evening until morning
except this one alone.
What is the reason?
The verse says:

phrases.aramaic: ״יַעֲרֹךְ אֹתוֹ אַהֲרֹן וּבָנָיו מֵעֶרֶב עַד בֹּקֶר״.
phrases.english: "Aaron and his sons shall arrange it from evening until morning."
phrases.notes: שמות כז:כא. The separate word "אותו", instead of "יערכנו", is what limits the law.

phrases.english: It is from evening until morning,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין דָּבָר אַחֵר מֵעֶרֶב עַד בּוֹקֶר.
phrases.english: and nothing else is from evening until morning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This gives the second reading of the ברייתא, which is the one that supports the answer in Step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That "אותו" sets the נרות apart from the general time rule.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The "דבר אחר" reading in the ברייתא on שמות כז:כא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The נרות are the only service valid all night, so they are an exception and are done after the פסח.

steps.title: The incense is linked to the lamps
steps.stepSummary: The קטרת is also an exception, because the תורה links it to the נרות with a הקש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the incense is compared to the lamps.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer to the question from Step 2. It explains why the קטרת, and not only the נרות, comes after the פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question in Step 2 named two services that have only 'בין הערבים': the קטרת and the נרות. Step 3 explained the נרות using the word אותו. Here the קטרת is tied to the נרות because the פסוק puts them together (שמות ל:ח), so the קטרת follows the same rule as the נרות.

keyTerms.meaning: a comparison the תורה makes by placing two things together, so they share rules

steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes the first ברייתא's answer completely. In that view, the פסח is brought before both the קטרת and the נרות.

phrases.english: And the incense is juxtaposed to the lamps.
phrases.notes: The verse is 'ובהעלות אהרן את הנרות בין הערבים יקטירנה'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the exception of the נרות (from אותו) to the קטרת through a הקש.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extending an exception by a הקש
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The קטרת has only 'בין הערבים', so it should come before the פסח.
steps.terutzMaskana: The קטרת is linked to the נרות, so it shares their status as a final service and comes after the פסח.

steps.title: A second ברייתא matches our original question
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches the order תמיד, קטרת, נרות, פסח. This is exactly what our question in Step 2 expected.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a ברייתא was taught in line with our difficulty: The תמיד comes before the incense. The incense comes before the lamps. And the lamps come before the פסח. Something described with both 'in the evening' and 'in the afternoon' should be pushed later than something described only with 'in the afternoon.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that one ברייתא actually holds the way our question in Step 2 assumed. In this ברייתא, the פסח comes after both the קטרת and the נרות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא applies the rule from Step 1 to every service with only 'בין הערבים'. It does not make an exception for the נרות. So it disagrees with the first ברייתא, and the גמרא must now explain how it handles the word אותו.

keyTerms.meaning: and it was taught in a ברייתא
like our difficulty, matching our question

steps.confusionAlert: 'כי קושיין' does not mean a new question. It means this ברייתא agrees with the question we asked in Step 2.

phrases.english: And it was taught in line with our difficulty:
The daily offering precedes the incense,
the incense precedes the lamps,
and the lamps precede the Paschal lamb.
Let an item about which it is said
'in the evening' and 'in the afternoon' be delayed
until after an item about which it is not said
anything but 'in the afternoon' alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second ברייתא that disagrees with the first one and supports the question from Step 2.
steps.raayaObject: The question in Step 2, that the קטרת and נרות should come before the פסח.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא giving the order תמיד, קטרת, נרות, פסח.

steps.title: But the verse says אותו
steps.stepSummary: How can the second ברייתא put the פסח after the נרות? The word אותו teaches that the נרות are the last service.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written 'אותו'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second ברייתא with the word אותו from Step 3 and Step 5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 learned from אותו that lighting the נרות is the only service valid through the night, so it should be last. If so, how can the second ברייתא put the פסח after the נרות?

phrases.english: But isn't 'it' written?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the second ברייתא using the source the first ברייתא relied on.
steps.kashyaTarget: The second ברייתא's order, which puts the פסח after the נרות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אותו excludes every other service after the נרות, and that should include the פסח.

steps.title: אותו only excludes the inside service, the incense
steps.stepSummary: In the second ברייתא, אותו excludes only a service done inside the היכל, which is the קטרת. It does not exclude the פסח, which is done outside in the עזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This 'אותו' is needed to exclude a service done inside. And what is it? The incense.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It narrows what the word אותו comes to exclude.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא read אותו as excluding every service after the נרות. The second ברייתא reads it as excluding only services inside the היכל, where the נרות are. The פסח is slaughtered outside in the עזרה, so it is not excluded.

keyTerms.meaning: he needs it (for a different teaching)
a service done inside the היכל

phrases.english: This 'it' is needed
to exclude a service performed inside,
and what is it? The incense.
phrases.notes: A short built-in question and answer.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי ״אוֹתוֹ״ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְמַעוֹטֵי עֲבוֹדָה שֶׁבִּפְנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by narrowing what אותו excludes.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redirecting the source (the word is needed for a different teaching)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אותו excludes every service after the נרות, including the פסח.
steps.terutzMaskana: אותו excludes only the inside service, the קטרת, from coming after the נרות.

steps.title: Why we needed the verse to exclude the incense
steps.stepSummary: Without אותו, we might have read the verse to mean: light the נרות first, then burn the קטרת. אותו rules that out.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: since it is written 'And when Aaron lights the lamps in the afternoon, he shall burn it,' we should light the lamps first and then burn the incense. So the Merciful One excluded this with 'אותו.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the mistake we would have made without the word אותו. This shows that the word is truly needed for the קטרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק mentions lighting the נרות and then burning the קטרת, so it sounds like the נרות come first. אותו teaches that nothing inside follows the נרות. So the קטרת must come before them.

keyTerms.meaning: it would have entered your mind to say

phrases.english: It could have entered your mind to say
since it is written
'And when Aaron lights the lamps
in the afternoon, he shall burn it,'
say: let us light the lamps first
and then burn the incense,
so the Merciful One excluded this with 'it.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the narrower reading of אותו is still needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the mistake we would have made without the word
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The order of the verse suggests the נרות first, then the קטרת.
steps.terutzMaskana: אותו teaches that the קטרת comes before the נרות.

steps.title: Then why does the verse say he burns it in the afternoon?
steps.stepSummary: If the קטרת comes before the נרות, why does the פסוק say 'בין הערבים יקטירנה' together with the lighting?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, why do I need 'in the afternoon he shall burn it'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what purpose the phrase in the פסוק serves, now that we know the קטרת comes first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase seems to tie the burning to the time of lighting, and that sounds like the opposite order. If the order is קטרת first, the phrase looks pointless or even misleading.

phrases.english: But then, 'in the afternoon he shall burn it'
why do I need it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם יַקְטִירֶנָּה לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading in Step 10 from the wording of the same פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that the קטרת comes before the נרות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse links the burning to the time of lighting, so the phrase seems useless or contradictory.

steps.title: The incense should already be burning when the lamps are lit
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק means the קטרת should already be burning on the מזבח at the time the נרות are lit.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the Merciful One is saying: at the time you light the lamps, the incense should be burning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the phrase is not about which comes first. It describes the קטרת already burning while the נרות are lit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'יקטירנה' here does not mean 'start burning it now.' It means the קטרת is in a state of burning. This fits the order קטרת first, then נרות, and the second ברייתא stands.

keyTerms.meaning: this is what the תורה means

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ברייתות. In the first, the פסח comes before the קטרת and נרות, because אותו makes the נרות last and the קטרת is linked to them. In the second, the order is תמיד, קטרת, נרות, פסח. There, אותו only excludes the inside service, and the קטרת is already burning when the נרות are lit.

phrases.english: This is what the Merciful One is saying:
at the time that you light the lamps
the incense should be burning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by reinterpreting the phrase in the פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'יקטירנה' means to start burning after the lighting.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means the קטרת is already burning during the lighting, so the קטרת comes first.

steps.title: Only the incense comes before the morning daily offering
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that nothing comes before the תמיד של שחר except the קטרת, because the קטרת's פסוק says 'בבקר בבקר.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Nothing comes before the morning daily offering except the incense alone, because the Torah says about it: 'In the morning, in the morning.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about the order of the morning services. It says the קטרת is the only service that comes before the תמיד של שחר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the תמיד של שחר is the first offering of the day. The ברייתא makes one exception, the קטרת, and bases it on the double wording 'בבקר בבקר' in its פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Incense burned on the golden altar
'In the morning, in the morning' (the double wording in the פסוק)

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לְךָ דָּבָר שֶׁקּוֹדֵם לְתָמִיד שֶׁל שַׁחַר
phrases.english: There is nothing that comes before the morning daily offering
except the incense alone,
because it says about it: 'In the morning, in the morning.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין לְךָ דָּבָר שֶׁקּוֹדֵם לְתָמִיד שֶׁל שַׁחַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new ברייתא on the same topic as before, the order of services in the בית המקדש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the קטרת comes before the תמיד של שחר.

steps.title: Why the double 'morning' puts the incense first
steps.stepSummary: The text explains the reasoning. The קטרת has 'בבקר בבקר' written about it, while the תמיד has only one 'בבקר.' So the קטרת comes first.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the incense should come first. The Torah says 'in the morning, in the morning' about it, as it is written: 'And Aaron shall burn on it incense of spices, in the morning, in the morning.' So it comes before something that has only one 'morning' written about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The text explains why the double word 'בבקר בבקר' means the קטרת goes before the תמיד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קטרת's פסוק says 'morning' twice. The תמיד's פסוק ('את הכבש אחד תעשה בבקר') says it only once. Something marked with a double 'morning' is treated as earlier in the morning than something marked with a single 'morning.'

phrases.english: And the incense should come first —
something about which it says 'in the morning, in the morning,'
as it is written: 'And Aaron shall burn on it'
'incense of spices, in the morning, in the morning,'
before something about which it does not say
anything but one 'morning.'
phrases.notes: This refers to the תמיד: 'את הכבש אחד תעשה בבקר' (במדבר כח:ד).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the source given in the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A service with a double 'morning' in its פסוק comes before a service with a single 'morning.'

steps.title: What may still be done after the afternoon daily offering
steps.stepSummary: The second half of the ברייתא lists what may come after the afternoon תמיד: קטרת, נרות, פסח, and a מחוסר כפורים on ערב פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: And nothing may be done after the afternoon daily offering except the incense, the lamps, the קרבן פסח, and a person missing his atonement offering on ערב פסח. He immerses a second time and eats his פסח at night.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives the afternoon rule. Almost nothing may be offered after the תמיד של בין הערבים, except a short list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תמיד של בין הערבים is supposed to close the day's offerings. Four exceptions are allowed: קטרת, נרות, the קרבן פסח, and a מחוסר כפורים on ערב פסח. That last person brings his late offering, immerses again, and can then eat his פסח at night.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who is pure but still must bring an offering before eating קדשים

steps.confusionAlert: A מחוסר כפורים is not impure anymore. He has already immersed. He is only missing his offering, which he needs before he may eat קדשים.

phrases.english: And there is nothing that is delayed
until after the afternoon daily offering
except the incense, the lamps, and the Pesach offering,
and one missing his atonement offering on the day before Pesach —
who immerses a second time
and eats his Pesach offering at night.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין לְךָ דָּבָר שֶׁמִּתְעַכֵּב אַחַר תָּמִיד שֶׁל בֵּין הָעַרְבָּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The afternoon counterpart to the morning rule in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only קטרת, נרות, פסח, and a מחוסר כפורים on ערב פסח may come after the afternoon תמיד.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל extends the exception to every day
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא says a מחוסר כפורים may bring his offering after the afternoon תמיד on any day of the year.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל, son of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא, says: Even a person missing his atonement offering on any other day of the year may bring it late. He immerses and eats holy food at night.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion in the ברייתא widens the last exception. It is not limited to ערב פסח but applies all year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא allowed the late offering only on ערב פסח. רבי ישמעאל allows it every day, so the person can eat קדשים that night. This sets up the גמרא's question in the next step.

keyTerms.term: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָא
keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who disagrees with the תנא קמא here
The rest of the days of the year

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָא אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka, says:
Also one missing his atonement offering
on the rest of the days of the year,
who immerses and eats holy food at night.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָא אוֹמֵר: אַף מְחוּסַּר כִּפּוּרִים בִּשְׁאָר יְמוֹת הַשָּׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the תנא קמא and widens his exception.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מחוסר כפורים may bring his offering after the afternoon תמיד on any day.

steps.title: What justifies רבי ישמעאל's exception?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the תנא קמא's view, because the פסח has כרת and so outweighs the מצוה of השלמה. But it asks why רבי ישמעאל lets an ordinary day override השלמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense according to the first opinion. The positive מצוה of the קרבן פסח, which carries כרת, comes and pushes aside the positive מצוה of completion, which does not carry כרת. But according to רבי ישמעאל, why is this positive מצוה stronger than that positive מצוה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי ישמעאל. It first explains why the תנא קמא's rule makes sense, then asks what reason רבי ישמעאל has.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a מצות עשה called השלמה: finish all offerings by the afternoon תמיד. On ערב פסח, the עשה of פסח, which carries כרת, is stronger and pushes השלמה aside. On a regular day, eating קדשים is just one עשה against another עשה. So why should it win?

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense (sets up a contrast before the challenge)
The positive מצוה to complete all offerings by the afternoon תמיד
What is its strength? (Why is it stronger?)

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule at work is that one עשה can push aside another only if it is stronger. Here כרת is what makes it stronger.

phrases.english: It makes sense according to the first opinion,
let the positive מצוה of Pesach come
which carries כרת,
and push aside the positive מצוה of completion
which does not carry כרת.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָא,
phrases.english: But according to Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka,
what makes this positive מצוה stronger
than that positive מצוה?!

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְתַנָּא קַמָּא, יָבֹא עֲשֵׂה דְפֶסַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the opinion of רבי ישמעאל stated in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ישמעאל's view that a מחוסר כפורים may bring his offering after the afternoon תמיד on any day.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One עשה can override another only if it is stronger. פסח is stronger because of כרת. Eating קדשים on a regular day is not stronger than השלמה, so it should not override it.

steps.title: רב חסדא: The case is a bird sin-offering
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers that רבי ישמעאל is talking about a person who brings a חטאת העוף. With that offering only the blood goes on the מזבח, so השלמה is not broken.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said in the name of רב חסדא: Here we are dealing with a bird sin-offering. With that offering, the only part that goes on the altar is its blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer to the question of Step 17. רבי ישמעאל is speaking about a מחוסר כפורים whose sin-offering is a bird.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of השלמה means nothing should be burned on the מזבח after the afternoon תמיד. A חטאת העוף has no parts that get burned; only its blood is put on the מזבח, and the כהנים eat the meat. So bringing it late does not break השלמה at all.

keyTerms.meaning: A sin-offering brought from a bird (for example, by a poor מצורע)

phrases.english: Ravina said that Rav Chisda said:
Here we are dealing with a bird sin-offering,
phrases.notes: This narrows רבי ישמעאל's ruling to a specific kind of offering.

phrases.english: where the altar gets only its blood.
phrases.notes: Nothing is burned, so השלמה is not affected.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 17 by limiting רבי ישמעאל's case to a bird sin-offering.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case limitation (אוקימתא): the ruling is set in a case where השלמה is not broken.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed רבי ישמעאל lets the person burn offering parts after the afternoon תמיד, which would break השלמה.
steps.terutzMaskana: He speaks of a חטאת העוף, where only blood goes on the מזבח, so nothing is burned after the תמיד.

steps.title: רב פפא: Even an animal sin-offering works, by leaving its parts overnight on the altar
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the case can even be an animal חטאת. The כהן brings its parts up to the top of the מזבח and leaves them there overnight, then burns them the next day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: You can even say the case is an animal sin-offering. The כהן brings its parts up and leaves them overnight on the top of the altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer. רב פפא does not need to limit the case to a bird.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רב פפא, the blood is sprinkled after the afternoon תמיד, but the fats are not burned that day. They stay overnight on top of the מזבח and are burned the next morning after the תמיד של שחר. That way the person is atoned for and השלמה is still kept.

keyTerms.meaning: A sin-offering brought from an animal
He brings it up and leaves it overnight

steps.confusionAlert: Normally, offering parts left overnight (לינה) become פסול. Here they are left on top of the מזבח itself, and in that place they stay kosher. That is why רב פפא's answer works.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Even if you say it is an animal sin-offering,
he brings it up and leaves it overnight on the top of the altar.
phrases.notes: The parts are burned the next day, after the morning תמיד.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא בְּחַטַּאת בְּהֵמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, wider answer to Step 17 that does not limit the case to a bird.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical method: the burning is pushed off to the next day, so השלמה stays intact.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought an animal offering would force burning after the afternoon תמיד.
steps.terutzMaskana: The parts wait overnight on top of the מזבח and are burned the next day.

steps.title: Challenge to רב חסדא: What about the guilt-offering?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that a מחוסר כפורים, such as a מצורע, also brings an אשם. רב פפא's method works for an אשם too, but רב חסדא's bird answer does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is also a guilt-offering! Granted, according to רב פפא, they leave it overnight on the altar. But according to רב חסדא, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב חסדא's answer. An אשם is always an animal, never a bird.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אשם must be a sheep, and its fats must be burned on the מזבח. רב פפא has no problem, because those parts can also wait overnight on top of the מזבח. רב חסדא's answer depended on the offering being a bird with only blood, so it does not cover the אשם.

keyTerms.meaning: Guilt-offering; a מצורע must bring one, and it is always an animal
Granted, it works out according to
What is there to say? (what answer is there)

phrases.english: But there is also a guilt-offering!
Granted, according to Rav Pappa,
that is fine, since they leave it overnight (on the altar),

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְרַב חִסְדָּא מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר?
phrases.english: but according to Rav Chisda, what can be said?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests both answers against the אשם. Only רב חסדא's answer is hurt.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's answer in Step 18 (the bird sin-offering)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A מחוסר כפורים also needs an אשם, which is always an animal with parts to burn. So the bird answer does not avoid breaking השלמה.

steps.title: Answer: His guilt-offering was already brought
steps.stepSummary: To defend רב חסדא, the גמרא says the case is a person who already offered his אשם earlier. Only the bird חטאת is left.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: The case is where his guilt-offering was already offered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב חסדא by narrowing the case even more. The אשם was already taken care of.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the אשם was already brought, the only thing still missing is the bird חטאת, which has only blood. So רב חסדא's answer stands again.

keyTerms.meaning: That his guilt-offering was already offered

phrases.english: They say: Where his guilt-offering was already offered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 20 on behalf of רב חסדא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the person still needed to bring his אשם, which has parts to burn.
steps.terutzMaskana: His אשם was already brought, so only the bird חטאת remains.

steps.title: Challenge: What about the burnt-offering, which also holds back atonement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that a מחוסר כפורים also brings an עולה. One might say a missing עולה does not hold back his atonement. But רבי ישמעאל himself says in a ברייתא that the עולה does hold it back, just like the חטאת and אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is also a burnt-offering! And if you say the burnt-offering does not hold back atonement, it was taught in a ברייתא that רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא says: Just as his sin-offering and guilt-offering hold him back, so too his burnt-offering holds him back!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem: the עולה, which is an animal burned completely on the מזבח. The next step answers this challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עולה is entirely burned, so bringing it after the afternoon תמיד would break השלמה. One could have answered that the עולה is not needed to finish atonement, so the person can bring it later. But רבי ישמעאל himself rules that the עולה is required, just like the חטאת and אשם, so that way out is closed.

keyTerms.meaning: Burnt-offering, burned completely on the מזבח
Holds back; prevents (the atonement from being complete)
And if you will say (blocking an expected answer)
But it was taught in a ברייתא

steps.whyThisMatters: This challenge uses רבי ישמעאל's own ruling against the answers given for him. It pushes the sugya to look for a new explanation.

phrases.english: But there is also a burnt-offering!
And if you say: the burnt-offering does not hold back (atonement),
phrases.notes: The גמרא names the expected escape so it can block it.

phrases.english: but it was taught in a ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָא אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka says:
phrases.notes: This is the same תנא whose ruling the sugya is explaining.

phrases.english: Just as his sin-offering and his guilt-offering hold him back,
so too his burnt-offering holds him back!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאִיכָּא עוֹלָה! וְכִי תֵּימָא: עוֹלָה לָא מְעַכְּבָא, וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the אשם problem was solved, the גמרא raises the עולה as a new, stronger problem.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that רבי ישמעאל's מחוסר כפורים can be atoned for without breaking השלמה (aimed at רב חסדא's bird answer, which only handles the חטאת)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The person still needs an עולה, which is burned completely on the מזבח. רבי ישמעאל himself says the עולה is required, so it cannot simply be left for later.

steps.title: Maybe his burnt-offering was already brought
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a way to save רב חסדא: the case is a person who already offered his עולה, so only the bird חטאת is left.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: the case is where his עולה was already offered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the last question the same way it answered the אשם problem: maybe the עולה was already brought earlier. It raises this idea only to test it in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 21 the גמרא said the אשם was already offered. Now it tries the same move for the עולה. If both were done, only the bird חטאת remains, and רב חסדא's answer works again.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you say (a suggested answer that is about to be tested)

phrases.english: And if you say: where his burnt-offering was already offered,
phrases.notes: Same move as step 21, where the אשם was already offered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes an answer to the עולה challenge of step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the עולה was already offered.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The missing עולה would block his atonement, which would break רב חסדא's bird-only answer.
steps.terutzMaskana: If the עולה was already done, only the bird חטאת is left. This answer is about to be challenged.

steps.title: Can the burnt-offering come before the sin-offering?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the suggestion: how could his עולה have been offered before his חטאת?
steps.simpleTranslation: But can his עולה be offered before his חטאת, which must come first?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the suggestion from step 23. The order of offerings does not seem to allow the עולה to go first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggestion only works if the עולה could be brought while the חטאת still waits. But the חטאת is supposed to be 'first.' So the case described in step 23 looks impossible. The proof comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: But is it really so? (a challenging question)

phrases.english: But can his burnt-offering be offered
phrases.notes: Asked in a surprised, challenging tone.

phrases.english: before his sin-offering, which comes first?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the עולה was already offered.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The חטאת must come before the עולה. So the עולה cannot already be done while the חטאת is still waiting.

steps.title: A ברייתא asks why the Torah says 'first'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא. It asks why the פסוק says the חטאת is 'first' when another פסוק already teaches that the עולה comes second.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: 'And he shall offer the one for the חטאת first.' Why does the פסוק say this? If it is to teach that the חטאת comes before the עולה, another פסוק already says: 'And the second he shall make an עולה, as is the rule.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts bringing proof for its challenge from a ברייתא. Here the ברייתא sets up a question. Its answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא notices that the order 'חטאת first, עולה second' is already clear from the later פסוק. So the word 'first' seems extra. An extra word in the Torah must teach something new.

keyTerms.meaning: But was it not taught in a בְּרַיְיתָא?
What does the פָּסוּק come to teach? (asked when a phrase seems extra)
As is the rule (the proper procedure)

steps.confusionAlert: Both פסוקים here (ויקרא ה) are about a bird חטאת and a bird עולה brought together. They are not about a מצורע. The ברייתא uses them to build a general rule.

phrases.english: But was it not taught in a baraita:
"And he shall offer the one for the sin-offering first,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא ה:ח

phrases.english: what does the verse come to teach?
If it is to teach that it comes before the burnt-offering,
it has already been stated:
"And the second he shall make a burnt-offering, as is the rule."
phrases.notes: ויקרא ה:י

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the source that backs up the challenge of step 24.
steps.raayaObject: That a חטאת must come before its עולה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading ויקרא ה:ח and ה:י.

steps.title: A general rule: every sin-offering comes first
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers: the extra word 'first' makes a general rule. Every חטאת comes before every עולה that is brought with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this verse sets a pattern for all חטאות: they come before all עולות that are brought with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question. The extra word 'first' is not about this one case. It sets up a rule for all offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בנין אב takes one case in the Torah and turns it into a pattern for similar cases. Here, the bird case teaches that anywhere a חטאת and an עולה come together, the חטאת goes first. That includes the מצורע.

keyTerms.meaning: Built a pattern (בִּנְיַן אָב): one case becomes the model for a general rule

phrases.english: Rather, this set a pattern
for all sin-offerings, that they come first,
before all burnt-offerings that come along with them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in step 25. It answers that ברייתא's internal question and so supplies the proof for the challenge of step 24.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the Torah adds the word 'first' (step 25).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is a בנין אב: every חטאת comes before every עולה that is brought with it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This general rule is the reason the suggestion of step 23 fails. A מצורע also brings a חטאת and an עולה together.

steps.title: Even a bird sin-offering comes before an animal burnt-offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds that even a bird חטאת comes before an animal עולה. So in רב חסדא's case, the עולה could not already have been offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we hold that even a bird חטאת comes before an animal עולה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its challenge. Even the 'weaker' bird חטאת still has to go before the 'bigger' animal עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think an animal offering is more important and could go first. But the rule holds even then. In רב חסדא's case the חטאת is a bird, so his עולה still could not come first. The answer of step 23 fails.
steps.whatToRemember: A חטאת must come before the עולה brought with it, even a bird חטאת before an animal עולה. So a person cannot normally have his עולה done while his חטאת is still waiting.

phrases.english: And we hold
that even a bird sin-offering
comes before an animal burnt-offering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the ברייתא's rule to רב חסדא's bird case and completes the challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer of step 23, that the עולה was already offered.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The חטאת always comes first, even a bird חטאת before an animal עולה. So the עולה cannot already be done while the bird חטאת waits.

steps.title: רבא: the burnt-offering of a מצורע is different
steps.stepSummary: רבא begins his answer: the עולה of a מצורע is a special case because of what the Torah says. The פסוק is quoted in the next part.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The עולה of a מצורע is different, because the Torah says:
steps.whatsHappening: רבא starts to defend the idea that the עולה was already offered. He says the מצורע is an exception. The line ends with 'the Torah says,' so the proof פסוק comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not reject the general rule that a חטאת comes first. He says the מצורע's עולה is a special exception to it. The source for this exception is the פסוק that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: A person with צָרַעַת who needs offerings to become fully pure

phrases.english: Rava said:
The burnt-offering of a leper is different,
because the Merciful One says:
phrases.notes: The פסוק continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 27 by making the מצורע an exception.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Exception case: the מצורע's עולה follows a special rule from a פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The general rule of a חטאת first would apply to a מצורע too, so his עולה could not already be done.
steps.terutzMaskana: The עולה of a מצורע is different, based on a פסוק (quoted next). So the case where his עולה was already offered may still be possible.
